{
  "rules": [
    "If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate and should be adjusted downward by 1–3% for the next 5–10 days.",
    "If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% to account for downward pressure or market panic.",
    "After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots and should be capped at +3% above peak for next 7–14 days.",
    "When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline after peak), model should reduce forecast slope by 20–50% for next 10 days.",
    "If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows rapid decline, sentiment history should trigger a 2–5% downward correction in next 3–7 days.",
    "For 30-day horizon, if model forecast is > 75% of true outcome’s 30-day average, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence bias.",
    "If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, -0.5, 0.67), model should be smoothed with a 3-day moving average to reduce noise.",
    "When true outcome deviates > 5% from model in first 5 days, adjust forecast by 1–2% per day for next 7 days to align with sentiment momentum."
  ]
}
